text:
Maria R.: quick sync — we're being asked to guarantee full physical separation of spans for a handful of customers (regulatory + contract). I sketched two approaches, want quick feedback before I write the RFC.

Ash K.: ok. what are the two?

Maria R.: (1) routing in the collector: route spans by `customer_id` to per-tenant exporters (S3/CH buckets) + per-tenant retention. Single collector process but many exporters configured dynamically.

Maria R.: (2) namespace-level segregation: tag spans with namespace, push into a shared exporter/DB but enforce RBAC and retention at query layer. cheaper but not physically separate.

Joel P.: my vote so far is for routing via the collector if any customers require "physical separation". mixing in the same DB complicates e-discovery + audit proofs.

Kevin L.: question: how many tenants do we expect to need full separation? if it's small (<10) routing to dedicated exporters is fine. if it's hundreds, per-tenant exporters explode config.

Maria R.: estimate: currently 3 contracts likely, another 5 in pipeline. not hundreds.

Ash K.: big caveat: how do we do dynamic provisioning of exporters without restarting collectors? we can either: (A) generate exporter configs and SIGHUP reload, (B) point routing to a proxy/agent that fans out to per-tenant endpoints, (C) route to a shard key and separate downstream storage ingestion.

Joel P.: (C) still means shared infra, just logical separation. For legal separation customers we need (A) or (B) + separate credentials.

Kevin L.: we could use a lightweight proxy service that accepts OTLP and forwards to a tenant-specific S3/CH writer based on token. That keeps the collector simple and enables per-tenant metrics on forwarding cost.

Zara (Legal): from a compliance standpoint we need clear chain-of-custody. Logical separation + RBAC is NOT enough for some regs. Physical export endpoints with separate KMS keys are preferable. Also retention must be enforceable by config, not by promise.

Maria R.: noted. so default = shared pipeline + RBAC for most; for a small set of "jurisdictional/high-risk" customers we provision per-tenant exporters with distinct KMS and storage.

Ash K.: sampling question: for per-tenant exporters, do we want uniform sampling rules? Some customers want full fidelity. We need to respect per-customer sampling config at ingestion time. That influences throughput sizing.

Maria R.: agreed. plan: attach `customer.id` and `customer.sampling_override` attributes at the app SDK or sidecar; collector routing and tail-sampling honors override if present.

Ash K.: rough pseudoconfig I threw together for OTEL collector routing processor:

```yaml
processors:
  batch:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: customer.id
        action: insert
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [attributes, batch, routing]
exporters:
  otlp/tenant-{customer.id}:
    endpoint: https://telemetry-forwarder.internal/tenant/{customer.id}
  otlp/shared:
    endpoint: https://telemetry-forwarder.internal/shared
processors.routing: # pseudo; route based on attribute
  rules:
    - from_attribute: customer.id
      match: "^(acct-[0-9]+)$"
      exporters: ["otlp/tenant-{customer.id}"]
    - default_exporters: ["otlp/shared"]
```

Kevin L.: that looks doable. question: where do we store retention policy and RBAC mapping? Console/db (per-customer record) or encoded in collector config?

Maria R.: prefer central config in Console + a short-lived signed token the collector/forwarder uses to decide route + KMS. avoids having to push collector config per change.

Joel P.: trade-offs: signed-token approach centralizes decisioning which helps ops. but the forwarder becomes a critical component; it must be highly available and audited.

Ash K.: agree; add tracing and metrics on the forwarder so we can show cost per-tenant and per-route. Also add quota enforcement before heavy processing to avoid someone blowing up a collector.

Zara (Legal): also document data residency per-tenant in Console UI. dropdown for "store_in: eu-west-1 / us-east-1 / dedicated-vpc". This must appear in contracts and be linked to operating runbooks.

Maria R.: good point. I'll add residency and KMS key id to tenant config. Collector/forwarder will require signed JWT referencing the tenant config and signed by Console key.

ops-bot: deploy triggered: telemetry/forwarder v2 -> staging (cf. deploy log: f3a9c).

Kevin L.: next engineering ask: put a small prototype forwarder in staging that accepts OTLP and records which exporter it would choose (dry-run) and per-tenant sample counts. we can loadtest with 1000 rps to validate CPU/mem.

Maria R.: timeline suggestion: prototype this sprint, RFC next week, implement per-tenant KMS + forwarder + Console UI over next 2 sprints for initial 3 customers.

Joel P.: nit: ensure alerts when forwarder starts dropping spans due to quota. Also produce a dashboard in Console: spans/sec by tenant, avg ingest latency, dropped count, sampling overrides.

Ash K.: I'll sketch the dashboard widgets: 1) ingest QPS (tenant) 2) tail-sample acceptance rate 3) storage writes/GB by tenant 4) retention expiry events.

Zara (Legal): please cc security and compliance when the RFC's draft is ready. I want to verify KMS + access logs.

Maria R.: thanks all — I'll draft RFC and prototype plan. will ping this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
